findings.quote: no one could say their treatment is adequate, so far as they develop them at all, because they have no material to work with
findings.problem: οὐκ ἂν εἴποι τις ἀξίως ἐφ᾽ ὅσον ἐξεργάζονται διὰ τὴν ἀπορίαν τῶν πραγμάτων: no one could adequately say how far they elaborate (work up) these topics, owing to their poverty of real material. The English turns 'worthily describe the extent' into a judgment that their treatment is inadequate and 'if at all'.
findings.proposed_fix: no one could adequately describe how far they work these up, given their lack of real material

findings.quote: even if I should seem inconsistent in my subject matter, in my handling of events, or in my style of expression
findings.problem: φανείημεν ἢ λήμμασι χρώμενοι τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἢ χειρισμῷ πραγμάτων ἢ τοῖς τῆς λέξεως ῥήμασι: if we appear to use the SAME themes, the same treatment of events, or the same turns of phrase (i.e. repetitiveness), not 'inconsistent'. Also the Greek has damaged text (οἷον εἰ τ̣...) just before.
findings.proposed_fix: for instance if I should appear to be using the same themes, or the same treatment of events, or the same turns of phrase

findings.quote: if I should sometimes slip in the names of mountains, rivers, or local places
findings.problem: ἐάν που παραπίπτωμεν ἐν ὀνομασίαις ὀρῶν ἢ ποταμῶν ἢ τόπων ἰδιότησι: if we anywhere make slips (fall into error) in the names of mountains or rivers or the particular features of places; 'slip in' reads as 'insert'.
findings.proposed_fix: if I should anywhere make slips in the names of mountains or rivers or in the particular features of places

findings.quote: the siege of Phanoteia or Coroneia or Haliartus
findings.problem: Greek has Φανοτείας καὶ Κορωνείας καὶ... ε... οῦ πολιορκίαν: the third name is lost in a lacuna (only fragments of letters); 'Haliartus' is invented and the list is 'and', not 'or'.
findings.proposed_fix: the siege of Phanoteia and Coroneia and [name lost in a gap in the text]

findings.quote: and beyond that to dwell on the capture of Tarentum, Corinth, Sardis, Gaza, Bactra, and, above all, Carthage
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) after πρὸς δὲ τούτοις before Τάραντος κατάληψιν; 'Corinth' is followed by a bracketed editorial supplement [πολιορκίαν]. The English reads on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: and beyond that [text missing] the capture of Tarentum, the [siege] of Corinth, Sardis, Gaza, Bactra, and above all the siege of Carthage

findings.quote: Again, other writers have gone on at length about the Syrian war.
findings.problem: Greek begins with a lacuna (***) then πάλιν ἕτεροι περὶ τοῦ Συριακοῦ πολέμου with no verb; 'have gone on at length' is supplied, not in the Greek.
findings.proposed_fix: [text missing] Again, others on the Syrian war.

findings.quote: what I have already explained more than once
findings.problem: ὅπερ ἡμῖν εἴρηται διὰ πλειόνων: what has been said by us at greater length (at some length), not 'more than once'.
findings.proposed_fix: what I have already explained at some length

units.note: Clause 'ἀλλ᾽ οὐ παντάπασιν εὐδοκεῖν ἐὰν ψιλῶς ... ἀποδιδῶμεν' is syntactically doubtful (infinitive with ἀλλ᾽ οὐ, subject unclear, probably corrupt or after a lacuna); the English silently makes the rival historians the subject ('they are not at all satisfied if we ...'). Ambiguity should be preserved; no fix proposed. Chapter has several gaps/damaged passages.
Last sentence (parma and Ligurian thyreoi): dative τῇ δυνάμει with ἀντεῖχον and the fragment's isolation make the sense somewhat ambiguous; the English is acceptable.

findings.quote: the rumor spread among many of Perseus’ Macedonians that it meant the king himself was being eclipsed
findings.problem: ἐπὶ Περσέως τοῦ Μακεδόνος ἐκράτησεν ἡ φήμη παρὰ τοῖς πολλοῖς ὅτι βασιλέως ἔκλειψιν σημαίνει: Μακεδόνος is singular, 'Perseus the Macedonian' (in the time of Perseus), and the belief prevailed among most people generally, not just his Macedonians; it signifies the eclipse of a king (general).
findings.proposed_fix: the belief prevailed among most people, in the time of Perseus the Macedonian, that it signified the eclipse of a king

findings.problem: εἰ καί τις ἄλλος: 'as much as anyone', i.e. he was as experienced in battles as anyone could be; 'like anyone else' makes him ordinary and drains the concession of καίτοι γε.

findings.quote: pretending that he was sacrificing to Heracles—fitting cowardly rites for a cowardly man, and prayers that the god would not accept
findings.problem: σκηψάμενος Ἡρακλεῖ θύειν, δειλὰ παρὰ δειλῶν ἱερὰ μὴ δεχομένῳ μηδ᾽ εὐχὰς ἀθεμίτους ἐπιτελοῦντι: the participles agree with Ἡρακλεῖ: Heracles does NOT accept cowardly sacrifices from cowards nor fulfil unlawful prayers. The English makes the rites 'fitting' and loses the negation on the god.
findings.proposed_fix: pretending that he was sacrificing to Heracles, a god who does not accept cowardly offerings from cowards nor fulfil unlawful prayers

findings.quote: while encamped in Thessaly for almost two years.
findings.problem: Greek breaks off here: σχεδὸν ἐπὶ δύ᾽ ἐνιαυτοὺς * ** with a lacuna before τὸ δὲ παρέντας; the English closes the sentence as if complete.
findings.proposed_fix: while encamped in Thessaly for almost two years [text missing here].

findings.quote: When the party led by Hegesipolis entered
findings.problem: Greek name is Ἁγέπολις (Hagepolis), not Hegesipolis.
findings.proposed_fix: When the party of Hagepolis entered

findings.quote: what the men around Hegesipolis said
findings.proposed_fix: what the men around Hagepolis said

findings.quote: For only in that way could a person show moderation even amid prosperity.
findings.problem: καὶ γὰρ οὕτω μόλις ἂν ἐν ταῖς εὐκαιρίαις ἄνθρωπον μέτριον ὄντα φανῆναι: even so (i.e. even with this mindfulness) a man would scarcely/hardly appear moderate in times of success; the English turns 'hardly even so' into 'only in that way'.
findings.proposed_fix: For even so, a man can hardly show himself moderate in times of prosperity.

findings.quote: because she has used these blessings with them too
findings.problem: διότι καὶ τούτοις ταῦτα τἀγαθὰ κέχρηκεν: κέχρηκεν is from χράω 'lend', Fortune has LENT these goods to them too, until she decides otherwise about them.
findings.proposed_fix: because she has lent these blessings to them too

findings.quote: whose name was scarcely known before
findings.problem: ὧν οὐδ᾽ ὄνομα πρότερον ἦν γνώριμον: whose very name was not (even) known before; 'scarcely' weakens the negation.
findings.proposed_fix: whose very name was not previously known

findings.quote: with Lycortas to command the infantry and Polybius the cavalry
findings.problem: ἡγεμόνα δὲ τῆς ὅλης συμμαχίας Λυκόρταν, τῶν δ᾽ ἱππέων Πολύβιον: Lycortas as commander of the whole allied force, not of the infantry only.
findings.proposed_fix: with Lycortas as commander of the whole allied force and Polybius of the cavalry

findings.quote: since Quintus Philippus was wintering in Macedonia.
findings.problem: The Greek breaks off mid-phrase: τὴν παραχειμασίαν ἐν τῇ (text ends; the place is not given). 'Macedonia' is supplied and the sentence closed.
findings.proposed_fix: since Quintus Philippus was wintering in the [text breaks off here]

units.note: Possible ambiguity: 'τὰ φιλάνθρωπα πρὸς τὴν βασιλείαν' (kindnesses toward the kingdom, by whom?) is read by the English as Achaean goodwill to Egypt; left as is.
